Corrections.RejectionReason: previous claim is not an exact audited-output quote

truthAudit.Summary: Run 2 identified 10 findings from the source. Of the 20 true vulnerabilities, Run 2 fully found 5 (SC-V3-001, SC-V3-004, SC-V3-006, SC-V3-010, and a related buffer overflow), partially found 2 (SC-V3-011 misclassified as CWE-330, SC-V3-013 misclassified as CWE-78), and missed 13 entirely. Run 2 also identified several legitimate issues not in the ground-truth list (format_string CWE-134, malloc null check CWE-476, admin exec command injection CWE-78). No findings were outright fabricated, but significant gaps exist in concurrency, recursion, integer arithmetic, and authentication-state coverage.

Items.Notes: Run 2 explicitly identified the format-string vulnerability in log_debug_message with CWE-134, quoting the exact anchors: runtime_log_format() and printf(active_format.c_str(), user_input). Matches the true vulnerability exactly.

Run 2 made no mention of the factorial computation or integer overflow. The source shows `long long result = 1; for (long long i = 2; i <= static_cast<long long>(x); i++) { result *= i; }` at lines 315-318, which can overflow for x >= 21. Run 2 did not identify this.

Run 2 made no mention of use-after-free in memory-pool cleanup. The source shows stage_deferred_history_flush (lines 813-828) allocating scratch from g_memory_pool and enqueueing lambdas that reference scratch, while cleanup() at line 884 calls g_memory_pool.cleanup() which frees all blocks — a classic UAF pattern. Run 2 did not identify this.

Items.PreviousOutputQuote: std::string validator_cmd = get_setting("validator_path", "/usr/bin/validator"); std::string config_file = get_setting("config_file", "default.conf"); std::string command = validator_cmd + " " + config_file; int result = system(command.c_str());
Items.Notes: Run 2 explicitly identified command injection in ConfigLoader::validate_config with CWE-78, quoting the exact anchors: validator_cmd, config_file, and system(command.c_str()). Matches the true vulnerability exactly.

Run 2 found a buffer-overflow issue in safe_string_copy (off-by-one null terminator), but did NOT identify the stack buffer overflow in evaluate_expression where `strcpy(input_buffer_, expression.c_str())` is called unconditionally when expression.length() >= sizeof(input_buffer_) (lines 831-832). The true vulnerability anchors (strcpy(input_buffer_; src_len > dest_size) are in a different code path than Run 2's finding.

Items.PreviousOutputQuote: long long old_value = value_; std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock(mutex_); value_ = old_value + 1;
Items.Notes: Run 2 explicitly identified the race condition in ThreadSafeCounter with CWE-362, quoting the exact anchors: old_value = value_ outside the lock, then value_ = old_value + 1 inside. Matches the true vulnerability exactly.

Run 2 made no mention of the logic bomb / emergency override bypass. The source shows at lines 592-598: if (login_attempts_ > 5) and input.find("EMERGENCY_OVERRIDE") then authenticated_ = true. Run 2 did not identify this CWE-511 issue.

Run 2 made no mention of path traversal in configuration loading. The source shows config_dir_ + filename at line 543 with no sanitization, allowing ../ sequences. Run 2 did not identify this CWE-22 issue.

Run 2 made no mention of heap overflow in the expression parser. The source shows buffer_size_ = 256 (line 367) and strcpy(expression_buffer_, expr_str.c_str()) at line 376 without bounds checking. Run 2 did not identify this CWE-122 issue.
Run 2 explicitly identified the hardcoded admin secret with CWE-798, quoting the exact anchor. Matches the true vulnerability exactly.

Items.PreviousOutputQuote: std::random_device rd; std::mt19937 gen(rd()); std::uniform_int_distribution<> dis(1000, 9999); return "TOKEN_" + std::to_string(dis(gen));
Items.Notes: Run 2 identified weak session token generation and quoted the correct anchors (std::mt19937, uniform_int_distribution, 1000, 9999). However, Run 2 classified it as CWE-330 (weak cryptography) instead of the correct CWE-338 (weak PRNG). The vulnerability was found but misclassified.

Run 2 made no mention of the thread-unsafe timestamp cache. The source shows `static std::tm cached_time;` at line 231 with `cached_time = *local_time` — localtime is not thread-safe. Run 2 did not identify this CWE-362 issue.

Items.PreviousOutputQuote: const char* temp_dir = std::getenv("TEMP"); std::string audit_path = std::string(temp_dir ? temp_dir : ".") + "\\supercalc_emergency.log"; std::string command = "cmd /C echo Admin override logged >> " + audit_path; system(command.c_str());
Items.Notes: Run 2 identified the insecure temp file handling but classified it as CWE-78 (command injection) rather than the correct CWE-377 (insecure temporary file). The evidence quote is accurate and covers the anchors (TEMP, TMPDIR, supercalc_emergency.log, system()). The vulnerability location was found but misclassified.

Run 2 made no mention of persistent authentication state. The source shows authenticated_, login_attempts_, and session_token_ as class members that persist across operations (lines 579-581). Run 2 did not identify this CWE-613 issue.

Run 2 made no mention of unhandled exception in variable parsing. The source shows `double value = std::stod(tokens[3]);` at line 729 inside handle_variable_command without a try-catch around that specific call (the outer try-catch at line 875 is in evaluate_expression, not handle_variable_command). Run 2 did not identify this CWE-754 issue.

Run 2 made no mention of integer underflow in memory-pool block split. The source shows `size_t remaining = previous_size - size - SPLIT_METADATA_BYTES;` at line 133, where previous_size < size + SPLIT_METADATA_BYTES causes unsigned underflow. Run 2 did not identify this CWE-191 issue.

Run 2 made no mention of unbounded recursion in the parser. The source shows parse_expression -> parse_factor -> parse_expression (lines 381-431) with PAREN_OPEN triggering recursive parse_expression calls and no depth limit enforced. Run 2 did not identify this CWE-674 issue.

Run 2 made no mention of data race in result cache. The source shows result_cache_ accessed in evaluate_cached (lines 445-452) without holding cache_mutex_ — the mutex is declared but never locked around cache reads/writes. Meanwhile thread_pool_->enqueue is used elsewhere. Run 2 did not identify this CWE-362 issue.

Run 2 made no mention of TOCTOU in config loading. The source shows std::filesystem::exists at line 544, then sleep_for at line 545, then std::ifstream file at line 546 — a classic TOCTOU window. Run 2 did not identify this CWE-367 issue.

Run 2 made no mention of integer division by zero in command routing. The source shows `return 100 / static_cast<int>(token_length);` at line 752 with no check that token_length != 0. Run 2 did not identify this CWE-369 issue.
